title: Excel tables: ranges that grow on their own

videos.script: Lesson five wrote E2 to E109 in every formula. One hundred and eight sales, typed into every range. {{ranges}} Then a new sale arrives, on row one hundred and ten. Every formula still stops at row one hundred and nine. Nothing shows an error. The totals are simply short. {{short}} An Excel table fixes that. Click inside the data, press Control T, and give the table a name. Sales. {{create}} Now a formula can say Sales, Bags, instead of E2 to E109. Read it aloud, and it says what it means. {{names}} And the table grows. Type a sale under the last row, and the table takes it in. Every formula that names the table counts one more sale. A formula column fills itself down. {{grow}} A total row adds up what the filter shows, and only that. {{total}} Lookups get safer too. A lookup into Products names the column it wants, so a column inserted there breaks nothing. {{lookup}} Every lesson after this one builds on three tables: Sales, Products and Customers. {{three}}
